climate.overview_html: Climate Week NYC 2026 is now open (September 20–27) with the official Opening Ceremony on Monday September 21, followed by the UNGA 81 General Debate starting Tuesday September 22 and the Secretary-General’s high-level climate summit on Wednesday September 23, which will focus on accelerating the just energy transition and mobilising affordable climate finance for developing countries. The backdrop is unchanged from yesterday: Foster & Rahmstorf’s >98%-confidence statistical confirmation that warming has accelerated faster than any prior decade in 177 years was published four days before the week opened; the Super El Niño is at or near seasonal peak (RONI +2.07°C, NDJ forecast +2.4–2.8°C); and Nepal’s UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission — the first directly implicating European-origin emissions in a Himalayan catastrophe — is active, framing the highest-stakes Climate Week since Paris.

items.source: Climate Group / UNGA / UN Secretary-General / Columbia Climate School
items.headline: Climate Week NYC 2026 Opens Today (September 20–27); Opening Ceremony September 21; UNGA 81 General Debate September 22–28; Secretary-General Convenes High-Level Climate Summit September 23 — Focus on Just Transition Finance and Developing-Country Adaptation
items.summary: Climate Week NYC 2026 officially opens today, September 20, with more than 1,000 events across New York City through September 27. The Opening Ceremony takes place Monday September 21, where senior government and industry leaders will set tone and announce commitments. Tuesday September 22 marks the start of the UNGA 81 General Debate, where heads of state and government address the Assembly through September 28. On Wednesday September 23, Secretary-General António Guterres convenes a high-level meeting on climate action and the just transition focused on three pillars: (1) accelerating a just and orderly energy transition to renewables; (2) mobilising and scaling up affordable climate finance and investments for developing countries, given investment needs of USD 3.1–3.5 trillion per year by 2030; and (3) delivering adaptation and resilience support in an era of climate overshoot. More than 130 of 194 parties to the Paris Agreement submitted new NDCs by March 27, 2026, covering close to 75% of today's energy-related GHG emissions. The EU has set a 66–73% reduction by 2035 relative to 1990; Japan targets 73% by 2040 relative to 2013. The Super El Niño peak, the Foster and Rahmstorf acceleration confirmation, and the Nepal–Tibet UNFCCC Loss and Damage submission all converge on what is expected to be the most politically charged climate week since Paris.

items.headline: WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update SON 2026: Niño 3.4 ~+3.6°C; Positive IOD +0.9°C; Above-Normal Temperatures Forecast Most Land Areas September–November; Super El Niño at Peak Season
items.summary: WMO's Global Seasonal Climate Update for September–November 2026 places the Niño 3.4 index at approximately +3.6°C above average, consistent with the confirmed Super El Niño at or approaching its seasonal peak. The co-occurring positive Indian Ocean Dipole at +0.9°C amplifies drought risk over Indonesia, the Philippines, and eastern Australia while increasing rainfall risk over eastern Africa and the Horn. Above-normal temperatures are forecast for most global land areas in SON 2026, with significant probability of record-breaking warmth in the tropics and sub-tropics. WMO confirms 2027 remains the likely warmest calendar year on record as the El Niño peak contribution propagates into NH winter 2026/27.

items.headline: Super El Niño Confirmed: Running ONI Crosses +2.0°C September 14 — First Super El Niño Since 2015–16; Peak Forecast NDJ 2026/27 at +2.4–2.8°C; WMO >95% Probability 2027 Sets Warmest Year Record
items.summary: The Running Oceanic Niño Index crossed the +2.0°C threshold on September 14, 2026, officially qualifying the current event as a Super El Niño — the first since 2015–16, which peaked at +2.6°C. The RONI reached +2.07°C. NOAA and WMO multi-model ensembles forecast a peak of +2.4–2.8°C for November–January 2026/27. Continued Atlantic hurricane suppression, drought in eastern Australia and SE Asia, and enhanced precipitation in the Horn of Africa are the primary near-term impacts. WMO assigns greater than 95% probability to 2027 exceeding 2024 as the warmest year on record.

items.headline: Europe Just Had Its Hottest Summer on Record — Western Europe 2.54°C Above 1991–2020 Normal; Rhine at 1880 Historic Low; 2,025+ Excess Deaths France; Farm Income Down ~9%; Paks and Cernavodă Nuclear Curtailed
items.summary: Analysis quantifies the cascading economic and humanitarian damage of Europe's record summer 2026 — the hottest in recorded history for western Europe at 2.54°C above the 1991–2020 Copernicus climatology. France recorded its hottest summer ever with 2,025+ excess deaths. The Rhine fell to its lowest navigational level since 1880, pushing freight costs 18–25% above seasonal norms. Low Danube water forced Hungary's Paks nuclear plant and Romania's Cernavodă plant to curtailed output. French farm income declined approximately 9% from crop failures.

items.headline: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse Floods ONGOING: ~1,446 Dead; ~6,669 Missing Including 587 Foreign Nationals; $820M+ Pledged; Nepal Climate Emergency Active; UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund Submission Initiated — First to Directly Implicate European Emissions in Himalayan Catastrophe
items.summary: Nepal's NDRRMA confirmed approximately 1,446 total deaths as of September 17, with approximately 6,669 persons missing including 587 foreign nationals from 34 countries. International pledges have reached $820 million. Nepal's parliament's national climate emergency declaration remains active. A formal UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission has been initiated — the first to directly implicate European-origin emissions in a documented Himalayan glacier catastrophe. ICIMOD's assessment found the Yanmarang Glacier lost approximately 40% of its volume since 2020. The event remains the deadliest glacier-related disaster in recorded Himalayan history.

items.source: Geophysical Research Letters / AGU / PIK Potsdam
items.headline: “Global Warming Has Accelerated Significantly” — Foster & Rahmstorf GRL Vol. 53 Issue 17; First Statistically Confirmed Acceleration Since ~2015 at >98% Confidence; Faster Than Any Prior Decade in 177-Year Record
items.summary: Foster and Rahmstorf apply natural-variability filtering across five global temperature datasets (NASA GISTEMP, NOAA GlobalTemp, HadCRUT5, Berkeley Earth, ERA5) to isolate the forced warming signal from ENSO, volcanic, and solar variability. The residual shows, for the first time with greater than 98% statistical confidence, that global warming has accelerated since approximately 2015 at a rate faster than any previous decade in the 177-year record. The implied non-linearity is consistent with compound forcing from cumulative CO₂, declining reflective aerosol loading as Asian coal combustion falls, and positive ice-albedo and water vapor feedbacks. The result directly strengthens the attribution basis for climate damage claims, including the Nepal–Tibet UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission active in this window.

items.headline: NOAA NCEI August 2026 Global Climate Report: Warmest August in 177-Year Record at +1.32°C; JJA 2026 Warmest Meteorological Summer Globally; 2026 On Track for Warmest Calendar Year
items.summary: NOAA confirmed August 2026 as the warmest August in 177 years of instrumental records at +1.32°C above the 20th-century average, breaking the prior tied record by 0.08°C. Meteorological summer (JJA) 2026 was the warmest on record globally at +1.21°C. Year-to-date (January–August 2026) global temperatures are the warmest in the 177-year dataset, placing 2026 on trajectory to become the warmest calendar year ever recorded.

items.headline: Copernicus August 2026 Bulletin: Joint-Hottest Month on Record (Tied July 2023) at 1.65°C Above Pre-Industrial; Extra-Polar SSTs All-Time August Record 21.07°C; 16th Consecutive Month ≥1.5°C
items.summary: Copernicus C3S confirms August 2026 as the world's joint-hottest month on record, tied with July 2023 at 1.65°C above the pre-industrial baseline. August 2026 was the 16th consecutive month at or above the 1.5°C Paris Agreement threshold. Extra-polar sea surface temperatures set an all-time August record at 21.07°C. 13.2% of global land and ocean surfaces registered record-high temperatures for any August day during the month.

weather.overview_html: The headline September 20 weather stories are Typhoon Dujuan’s final approach and the Atlantic’s first named storm. Dujuan was located 761 km SSW of Yokosuka at 0300 UTC September 20, moving NNW at 7 km/h with central pressure 970 hPa and maximum sustained winds of 35 m/s (126 kph) with gusts to 50 m/s; the system is forecast to approach the Kanto region early September 21 morning before curving NNE and becoming extratropical by September 22. Tokyo Game Show 2026 cancelled its final day (Monday September 22) on September 19 due to Dujuan, offering refunds and online streams for affected stage events — the longest-ever TGS, originally running five days, is curtailed a day early. The 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya remain on high alert for September 20–21 medal events, with approximately 4,000 delegation participants housed on a cruise ship in Nagoya port. In the Atlantic: Tropical Depression Six formed SW of the Azores on September 19 and is forecast to reach Tropical Storm Fay strength (65–75 kph) by September 20 UTC; the NHC expects gradual weakening and post-tropical transition by September 22 with no hazards to land — the season’s 6th named storm and still the first season without a hurricane since records began in the satellite era. All other events (SE Asia haze, European wildfires, Nepal floods, Pakistan monsoon) show no material new update as of September 20 morning.

items.source: Japan Times / JMA / Kotaku / Business Standard / Asian Games Nagoya OC
items.headline: Typhoon No. 25 Dujuan UPDATED September 20: 761 km SSW of Yokosuka, 970 hPa, 35 m/s Winds; Kanto Approach Early September 21; Tokyo Game Show Final Day (Monday) Cancelled; Asian Games Nagoya High Alert Continues; Extratropical September 22
items.summary: As of 03:00 UTC September 20, Typhoon No. 25 Dujuan was located approximately 761 km south-southwest of Yokosuka, Japan, tracking north-northwestward at 7 km/h. Central pressure: 970 hPa. Maximum sustained winds: 35 m/s (126 kph). Maximum gusts: 50 m/s. Maximum significant wave height: 8.5 metres. JMA forecast: the system approaches the Izu Islands on September 20 and the Kanto coastal region early September 21 morning before curving NNE toward the Pacific, passing east of Kanto and weakening to extratropical by September 22. Expected rainfall: up to 200 mm in 24 hours over Kanto and the Izu Islands on September 20–21. On September 19, organisers of Tokyo Game Show 2026 cancelled the event's final day (Monday September 22), citing intensifying wind and rain and transport disruptions — organising online broadcasts for affected stage events and issuing refunds for 8,700 Monday tickets. The 2026 Asian Games (Nagoya, September 19–October 4) remain on high alert for September 20–21 medal events; approximately 4,000 delegation participants are on a cruise ship in Nagoya port. Nagoya's forecast is less severe than Tokyo's — mostly cloudy conditions with lower direct precipitation probability.

items.headline: Tropical Storm Fay Forms in Open North Atlantic — TD 6 Strengthens to Named Storm September 19–20; Max Winds 65–75 kph; SW of Azores; No Land Threat; Post-Tropical September 22; 2026 Season’s 6th Named Storm; Latest-Season Zero-Hurricane Record Continues
items.summary: Tropical Depression Six formed southwest of the Azores at approximately 15:00 UTC September 19, 2026, with initial maximum sustained winds of 55 km/h and minimum central pressure 1009 hPa. NHC forecast the depression to reach tropical storm strength (Tropical Storm Fay) by 00:00 UTC September 20, with maximum winds reaching 65–75 km/h by 00:00 UTC September 21. The system is forecast to track generally northeastward over the open North Atlantic with no coastal watches or warnings in effect and no land hazards identified. Gradual weakening is forecast after brief peak intensity, with post-tropical transition expected September 22. Fay becomes the 2026 Atlantic season's sixth named storm. The season has still produced zero hurricanes through September 20 — record-breaking: the previous latest first hurricane was 1966 in the satellite era, and the 60-year record for season start was broken September 18.

items.source: Time / ASMC ASEAN / Mongabay / ABC News Australia
items.headline: SE Asia Wildfire Haze ONGOING: 12 Million People Blanketed; 113,336 Respiratory Cases Indonesia (Sept 9); Japan CH-47 Chinooks Kalimantan Sept 12–19; Worst Indonesian Wildfires in 11 Years; Fires Through October/November
items.summary: No material update September 18–20. Status as of September 17: more than 12 million people blanketed in thick smog across Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam. Indonesia's Health Ministry recorded 113,336 respiratory infection cases across seven provinces as of September 9. At least 200,000+ hectares burned across Borneo and Sumatra. Japan CH-47 Chinooks remained deployed in West Kalimantan through September 19. On September 14 Kuala Lumpur, Singapore, and Kuching ranked 1–3 globally for worst air quality. ASEAN Level 3 (highest) alert remains active. Indonesian authorities warn fires could continue through October or early November under Super El Niño-driven late rainy season suppression.

items.headline: Europe Wildfires ONGOING: 668,035 ha Burned Per EFFIS (As of September 16–17); Nearly Double 20-Year Average of 346,567 ha; Worst Season Since 2017; Extreme Fire Danger Continues Iberian Peninsula and Western Balkans
items.summary: No new EFFIS update as of September 20. Status as of September 16–17: 668,035 hectares burned in Europe in 2026, nearly double the 20-year average (2006–2025) of 346,567 hectares. Worst wildfire season since 2017. Extreme fire danger continues in the Iberian Peninsula, Pyrenees, and western Balkans. The season is driven by western Europe's hottest summer on record (2.54°C above the 1991–2020 average) and drought accumulating from early spring.

items.headline: Pakistan NDMA Flood Alert ONGOING: Monsoon Death Toll 234+ Dead / 596+ Injured; GB, KPK, Punjab, Balochistan Flash Flood Risk; Final Monsoon Active Phase Through Late September
items.summary: No new NDMA update found September 18–20. Status as of September 15: nationwide monsoon death toll 234 dead and 596 injured since late June. Flash flood risks cover Gilgit-Baltistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab, and Balochistan. Urban flooding continues in Lahore, Faisalabad, and Rawalpindi. Final monsoon active phase extends through late September.

renewables.overview_html: The week’s flagship grid infrastructure contract remains 50Hertz awarding NSORe + Siemens Energy the LanWin3 2 GW North Sea HVDC offshore converter platform on September 18 — NSORe’s second 2 GW 50Hertz contract in 2026, combined LanWin3 + LanWin6 value approximately €2.5 billion. Africa adds its most significant new contract: EnerSynk + ZESCO’s 25-year, 500 MW Zambia Copperbelt PPA signed September 16 — the country’s largest-ever renewable contract, replacing drought-hit Zambezi hydropower for the copper-mining industry. In Europe: UK DCO consent for Morecambe (480 MW) + Morgan (September 15); Econergy’s €134.3 million entry into France via the Escofi 740 MW wind platform (September 15); and Masdar + Luxcara’s €5 billion+ Germany offshore wind + BESS MoU (September 14). Earlier in the window: Gennaker 976.5 MW Baltic Sea financial close at €3 billion+ (September 11) and India’s 16.39 GW in April–July 2026, on track for a record ~50 GW annual pace.

items.headline: 50Hertz Awards LanWin3 2 GW North Sea HVDC Converter Platform Contract to NSORe + Siemens Energy — Second 2 GW NSORe/50Hertz Contract in 2026; Combined LanWin3 + LanWin6 Value ~€2.5 Billion to NSORe; Topside Rostock-Warnemünde, Jacket Vlissingen
items.summary: German transmission system operator 50Hertz awarded the LanWin3 North Sea offshore HVDC converter platform contract to the Neptun Werft–Smulders Offshore Renewables (NSORe) joint venture and Siemens Energy on September 18. This is NSORe's second major 50Hertz contract in 2026, following the LanWin6 award in June. Siemens Energy supplies the high-voltage components; NSORe handles system design, procurement, construction, offshore installation, and commissioning. The topside is fabricated at Neptun Werft in Rostock-Warnemünde, Germany; the steel jacket at Smulders in Vlissingen, the Netherlands. Combined contract value attributable to NSORe for LanWin3 and LanWin6 totals approximately €2.5 billion. LanWin3 is part of Germany's programme to connect the offshore wind build-out in the North Sea to the onshore grid at scale, with Germany's 2026 offshore tenders requiring co-located battery storage.

items.headline: Zambia Inks 25-Year PPA for 500 MW Solar Project — EnerSynk + ZESCO Copperbelt; Zambia’s Largest-Ever Renewable Contract; Replaces Drought-Hit Zambezi Hydropower for Copper Industry
items.summary: EnerSynk and ZESCO Ltd signed a 25-year PPA on September 16 for a 500 MW solar PV project in Zambia's Copperbelt — the country's largest-ever renewable energy contract. The project specifically targets the copper-mining industry's power supply chain, which accounts for approximately 70% of Zambia's total power demand. The plant reduces ZESCO's dependence on hydropower repeatedly curtailed in 2026 by drought driven by the positive IOD and Super El Niño.

items.headline: UK Secretary of State Approves DCO for Morecambe (480 MW) + Morgan Offshore Wind Transmission Assets — Full Consent Package Complete; Export Cables, Substations + Grid to Penwortham; >500,000 UK Households
items.summary: UK Secretary of State approved the Development Consent Order for transmission assets serving both the 480 MW Morecambe and co-located Morgan offshore wind farms on September 15. The consent covers offshore export cables, landfall infrastructure, onshore cables, substations, and grid connection to the National Grid substation at Penwortham, Lancashire, completing the full regulatory package for Morecambe. The 35-turbine project will power over 500,000 UK households.

items.source: Renewable Energy Magazine / reNEWS / Yahoo Finance
items.headline: Econergy Acquires Escofi — 740 MW French Onshore Wind Platform for €134.3 Million: 128 MW Operational, 34 MW Under Construction, 578 MW in Development; >90% Operating Capacity Under 20-Year French CfDs at >€80/MWh; Econergy’s Entry into France
items.summary: Econergy Ltd acquired Escofi, a private French onshore wind developer founded in 1988, for €134.3 million on September 15 — Econergy's entry into France. Escofi's 740 MW portfolio: 128 MW operational, 34 MW under construction (target 2027), 147 MW advanced development, and 432 MW early-to-mid development. More than 90% of operational and under-construction capacity benefits from 20-year French CfDs at above €80/MWh.

items.source: offshoreWIND.biz / Energy Storage News / Energy Global
items.headline: Masdar + Luxcara Sign €5 Billion+ MoU for Germany Battery Storage and Offshore Wind — Signed During UAE State Visit to Berlin; Potential Expansion to Other European Markets
items.summary: Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company (Masdar) and Luxcara signed an MoU on September 14 to explore joint investment in excess of €5 billion in battery energy storage systems and offshore wind in Germany, announced during the UAE state visit to Berlin. Germany's 2026 offshore wind tenders require co-located BESS, driving this market. The partnership targets co-development, financing, and ownership, with possible expansion to other European markets.

items.headline: Skyborn Renewables + Stadtwerke München Close €3 Billion+ Financing for 976.5 MW Gennaker Offshore Wind (German Baltic Sea) — Amazon 600 MW PPA; Uniper 100 MW PPA; SWM 25% Equity; Target Commercial Operations End-2028
items.summary: Skyborn Renewables and Stadtwerke München reached financial close on September 11 for the 976.5 MW Gennaker offshore wind farm in the German Baltic Sea. Total financing: €2.1 billion non-recourse project finance from 16 commercial lenders and the EIB, mobilising over €3 billion total investment. PPAs: 600 MW to Amazon, 100 MW to Uniper. SWM holds 25% equity. 63-turbine Siemens Gamesa project, target commercial operations end-2028.

items.headline: Enel Green Power Acquires Faraday (682 MW DC, Utah) + Skyhawk (128 MW DC, Tennessee) From Excelsior Energy Capital for $760 Million — PacifiCorp 20-Year PPA; Meta Energy Off-take; TVA Contract
items.summary: Excelsior Energy Capital completed the $760 million sale of Faraday Solar (682 MW DC, Utah, 20-year PacifiCorp PPA with Meta energy attribute purchase) and Skyhawk Solar (~128 MW DC, Tennessee, TVA long-term PPA) to Enel Green Power North America on September 11. Combined ~810 MW DC / 625 MW AC of contracted U.S. solar capacity. Following the acquisition, Enel is expected to have over 13 GW of renewable wind, solar and storage capacity in North America.

items.headline: India Renewable Additions: 16.39 GW in April–July 2026 (14.33 GW Solar + 2.04 GW Wind); BESS Growing Faster Than Generation; On Track for ~50 GW Annual FY2026–27
items.summary: India added 16.39 GW of renewable energy capacity in the first four months of FY2026–27 (April–July 2026): 14.33 GW solar PV and 2.04 GW wind. Battery energy storage additions are growing faster on a percentage basis than either solar or wind, reflecting MNRE's push to pair storage with large-scale renewable plants. The run rate places India on track for approximately 50 GW of annual additions in FY2026–27 — which would be a record.

science.overview_html: The window’s central climate science result remains Foster & Rahmstorf GRL Vol. 53 Issue 17 (September 16): >98%-confidence acceleration of the forced warming trend since ~2015, faster than any prior decade in the 177-year record across five datasets. The digest’s most consequential new addition is arXiv:2609.03582 — Google DeepMind & Google Research’s WeatherNext 3, which breaks two foundational constraints of current AI weather models: it trains directly on raw weather station observations (not reanalysis grids) and live geostationary satellite mosaics, producing hourly 0.05° (~5 km) forecasts for surface temperature and dew point, 0.1° for other surface variables, re-initialising every hour; now live in Google Search, Maps and Earth Engine. The ensemble calibration frontier carries forward: SPW — zero-marginal-cost calibrated ensembles from any deterministic ML model at inference time and BEAST — 96-member Bayesian weight-space ensemble on JUPITER (3.96 EFLOP/s), competitive with ECMWF AIFS on extreme weather metrics. Stratospheric chemistry: van Herpen et al. Nature Communications on Hunga Tonga’s Cl-radical CH4 oxidation pathway at 900±220 Mg/day, absent from CMIP7 models and with implications for stratospheric aerosol injection scenarios.

items.source: Geophysical Research Letters / AGU / PIK Potsdam
items.headline: GRL Vol. 53 Issue 17: “Global Warming Has Accelerated Significantly” — Foster & Rahmstorf; First Statistically Confirmed Acceleration Since ~2015 at >98% Confidence; Faster Than Any Prior Decade in 177-Year Record After ENSO/Volcanic/Solar Removal Across Five Temperature Datasets
items.meta: Foster & Rahmstorf · Geophysical Research Letters (2026) · Vol. 53, Issue 17 · doi:10.1029/2025GL118804 · Published 16 September 2026
items.summary: Foster and Rahmstorf apply natural-variability filtering across five global temperature datasets (NASA GISTEMP, NOAA GlobalTemp, HadCRUT5, Berkeley Earth, ERA5) to isolate the forced warming signal from ENSO, volcanic, and solar variability. The residual shows, for the first time with greater than 98% statistical confidence, that global warming has accelerated since approximately 2015 at a rate faster than any previous decade in the 177-year record. The implied non-linearity is consistent with compound forcing from cumulative CO₂, declining reflective aerosol loading as Asian coal combustion falls, and positive ice-albedo and water vapor feedbacks. The result directly strengthens the attribution basis for climate damage claims, including the Nepal–Tibet UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission active in this window — framing it as the capstone scientific finding of Climate Week NYC 2026.

items.headline: WeatherNext 3 (arXiv 2609.03582) — Google DeepMind + Google Research: Hourly 0.05° (~5 km) Surface Forecasts from Raw Weather Station Observations + Live Geostationary Satellite Mosaics; Breaks Reanalysis Dependence; Live in Google Search, Maps, Earth Engine
items.meta: Lam et al. · Google DeepMind / Google Research · arXiv:2609.03582 · September 3, 2026 · cs.LG / physics.ao-ph
items.summary: WeatherNext 3 addresses two foundational shortcomings of current AI weather models: (1) lower spatial/temporal resolution than the best physics-based models, and (2) exclusive initialisation with and training on reanalysis data, meaning they cannot directly use raw observations and inherit any reanalysis bias. WeatherNext 3 trains dedicated observational heads on raw weather station measurements and takes a live global geostationary satellite mosaic as a direct model input, re-initialises every hour, and emits forecasts at 0.05° (~5 km) for surface temperature and dew point, 0.1° for other surface variables (wind at 10 km), and 0.25° for pressure levels. The model uses a FGN (Fourier-Grid-Neural) mesh transformer architecture with live satellite assimilation. The system is already deployed in Google Search weather, the Gemini app, Google Maps, the Maps Platform Weather API, and Google Earth Engine. WeatherNext 3 represents the first large-scale AI weather model to achieve hourly re-initialisation by directly ingesting live satellite data alongside conventional observations.

items.headline: Nature Communications: Hunga Tonga Stratospheric Aerosol Layer Catalysed Anomalous CH<sub>4</sub> Oxidation at 900±220 Mg/day Via Cl-Radical Pathway — 12 ppb HCHO at 30 km; Pathway Absent From CMIP7 Models; Potential Net Cooling Offset in Large-Eruption/SAI Scenarios
items.meta: van Herpen et al. · Nature Communications (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41467-026-72191-4 · Published 15 September 2026
items.summary: Van Herpen et al. show that the 2022 Hunga Tonga eruption's stratospheric sulphate aerosol layer catalysed a previously uncharacterised methane-oxidation pathway involving Cl radicals produced at aerosol surfaces. Using ACE-FTS and MIPAS limb-emission satellite observations, the authors quantify CH₄ oxidation at 900 ± 220 Mg/day between 25–35 km altitude, sufficient to explain the anomalous HCHO column of ~12 ppb at 30 km (~8× background). The mechanism is absent from current CMIP7 chemistry–climate models; if triggered by large eruptions or proposed stratospheric aerosol injection, it could constitute a net cooling offset not captured in climate sensitivity assessments or geoengineering scenario modelling.

items.source: arXiv / Jülich Supercomputing Centre / JUPITER / Helmholtz AI
items.headline: arXiv 2609.12815 (BEAST): Bayesian Ensemble AI Swin Transformer on JUPITER (20,480 NVIDIA GH200 GPUs, 3.96 EFLOP/s); 700M Parameters; 96-Member Weight-Space Ensemble; Competitive With ECMWF AIFS on Extreme Weather Metrics
items.summary: BEAST (Bayesian Ensemble AI Swin Transformer) is trained on the JUPITER supercomputer — first exaflop-class European HPC (20,480 NVIDIA GH200 Grace Hopper Superchips, 3.96 EFLOP/s). The 700-million-parameter model generates 96 ensemble members via weight-space sampling. On benchmark evaluations for extreme weather events, BEAST achieves skill competitive with ECMWF's AIFS and operational NWP ensemble systems. Directly addresses the central limitation of deterministic AI weather models: underrepresentation of forecast uncertainty for low-probability high-impact events.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.08412 — Stochastically Perturbed Weights (SPW): Zero-Marginal-Cost Calibrated Ensembles From Deterministic ML Weather Models (Aurora, GraphCast, SFNO, AIFS); CRPSS 0.04–0.13 Below Trained-Probabilistic Baselines at 10-Day Lead
items.meta: Adamov et al. · arXiv:2609.08412 · Submitted to Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems (AMS) · September 2026
items.summary: Adamov et al. propose Stochastically Perturbed Weights (SPW), a method for generating calibrated probabilistic ensembles from any deterministic ML weather model by perturbing the network's weight tensors at inference time — requiring zero additional training computation. Tested across Aurora, GraphCast, SFNO, and AIFS backbones, benchmarked against trained-probabilistic models. At 240-hour lead times, SPW ensembles achieve CRPSS 0.04–0.13 below the best trained-probabilistic baseline with no marginal training cost. Key limitation: the productive injection site is architecture-specific, making SPW a per-model tuning procedure rather than a universal plug-and-play recipe.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.10135 — Agent-Based ML–LLM Fusion with Self-Optimizing Prompts for Plateau Weather Alerts: Automated Natural-Language Alert Generation for Qinghai–Tibet Complex Terrain; Outperforms Fixed Templates on Specificity and User Comprehension
items.summary: This paper proposes an agent-based architecture combining an ML-driven weather prediction model with a large language model for automated generation of weather alert text for the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau — a region where complex orography, data sparsity, and rapidly shifting convective systems make traditional NWP and fixed-template alerting underperform. The ML agent ingests numerical forecast outputs and hazard probability fields; the LLM agent translates these into natural-language alert bulletins using self-optimizing prompt chains that adapt to the evolving forecast state. Evaluations show improved alert specificity and user comprehension scores compared to rule-based text generation baselines.

items.headline: Nature Geoscience: “A Strengthening Yet Less Extreme Atlantic–European Jet During Winter” — 300-Year Record (1725–2100); Jet Strengthened 0.13 SD Since Pre-Industrial; Projected to Continue Strengthening But With Fewer Extreme Excursions; Implications for European Windstorms and Blocking
items.meta: Brönnimann, Brugnara & Kallabis · Nature Geoscience (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41561-026-02069-z · Published 10 September 2026
items.summary: Brönnimann, Brugnara, and Kallabis present a 300-year analysis of Atlantic–European jet stream variability using four long European pressure records combined with climate model ensemble projections. Since pre-industrial, the jet has strengthened 0.13 SD and shifted poleward. Future projections show continued strengthening through 2100 but with extremes becoming less frequent — the counterintuitive result that a stronger mean jet has reduced variance in its most anomalous states. Key implication: the most destructive European windstorms and the most persistent blocking-driven heat waves may become less frequent even as mean circulation intensifies.

items.source: arXiv / Bjerknes Centre for Climate Research / University of Bergen
items.headline: arXiv 2609.11696: WRF Dynamical vs Diffusion-Model Generative Downscaling for Subseasonal Extreme Precipitation at 3-Week Lead Times — WRF Wins Non-Stationary Multicell Events; Diffusion More Consistent on Stationary Supercells; Both Beat Raw ECMWF
items.summary: Head-to-head evaluation of WRF dynamical downscaling versus a diffusion-based deep generative model, downscaling ECMWF subseasonal forecasts for two physically distinct extreme precipitation events at leads up to 3 weeks. Both substantially improve on raw ECMWF outputs. WRF achieves highest probabilistic skill for a multicell non-stationary event. The diffusion model outperforms WRF on a stationary supercell event and is more consistent across metrics overall, suggesting regime-adaptive or ensemble downscaling frameworks for operational S2S extreme precipitation prediction.

items.title: Mazama Energy Raises $135 Million Series B for Superhot Engineered Geothermal — Led by Centaurus Capital + Doerr Capital; ConocoPhillips, Shell Ventures, Khosla, Gates Frontier Co-Invest; Newberry Volcano, Oregon; Project Athena Drilling 750°F (400°C) Target
items.body_html: Mazama Energy, the Newberry Volcano (Oregon) superhot engineered geothermal system developer, raised $135 million in an oversubscribed Series B announced September 17, co-led by Centaurus Capital (John Arnold’s fund) and Doerr Capital. ConocoPhillips, Shell Ventures, Khosla Ventures, Gates Frontier, SiteGround Capital, H. Barton Asset Management, and the Jeffrey and Marieke Rothschild Foundation also participated. Mazama holds the record for the hottest engineered geothermal system ever built: a 629°F (331°C) EGS at Newberry in 2025, proving reservoir creation, connectivity, and heat recovery. Its second well, Project Athena, reached 10,350 feet in 15 days — 80% faster than the 2025 well — and is drilling a further mile toward a 750°F (400°C) target; at that temperature a single well delivers up to 10× the power of a conventional 390°F (200°C) well while using 75% less water and 80% fewer wells. The raise reflects growing major-oil-company conviction that superhot geothermal, with its baseload output profile and minimal surface footprint, can anchor firm-power supply in a grid increasingly dominated by variable renewables.

items.title: EU Climate Insurance Alliance — Von der Leyen State of the Union September 16: Only 25% of European Catastrophe Losses Currently Insured; Parametric + Group Instruments Proposed; 100 Vulnerable EU Regions to Be Mapped by October; Alliance Faces Criticism for Lacking Mandatory Cover Mandate
items.body_html: European Commission President von der Leyen announced the European Climate Insurance Alliance in her September 16 State of the Union address, citing data showing that only 25% of European catastrophic climate losses are currently covered by insurance — a structural gap that leaves households, farmers, and municipalities absorbing the remainder and creates sovereign fiscal risk during compound extreme-weather years. The Alliance will bring together insurers, investors, risk modellers, regulators, and policyholders to develop group insurance pools for currently uninsurable catastrophe risks and expand parametric insurance instruments — paying on measurable thresholds such as rainfall levels or temperatures rather than assessed losses — for agriculture, coastal flooding, and wildfire; the European Commission will map the 100 most-vulnerable EU regions by October 2026. The announcement follows Europe’s wildfire season reaching 668,035 ha per EFFIS September 17 with uninsured losses estimated at €40–60 billion. Critics said the Alliance would not close the protection gap without mandatory natural-hazard cover.

items.title: Laki Power Raises €6 Million Series A Led by NATO Innovation Fund — Iceland Grid Monitoring Device Self-Powered From Live HV Lines; NIF’s First Iceland Investment; + ReykVC
items.body_html: Laki Power, a Reykjavík-based grid monitoring hardware company, closed a €6 million Series A on September 16 led by the NATO Innovation Fund with co-investment from ReykVC — NIF’s first investment in an Icelandic company. Laki Power’s core product is a grid monitoring device that harvests its operating power directly from live high-voltage transmission lines via inductive energy harvesting, eliminating the need for external power supplies, batteries, or fibre-optic ground wires. The device provides real-time line-current, temperature, sag, and fault-location data to grid operators; the self-powered design makes it viable for remote high-voltage corridors where conventional monitoring costs are prohibitive, directly relevant to Nordic and Arctic grid resilience and the NATO dual-use energy security priority driving NIF’s participation.
